create.name: Andrew Chapman
create.bio:
Andrew Chapman is a Buddhist meditation teacher in Nashville who has been at the heart of Wild Heart Meditation Center since its early years. He trained under the centre's founder, Dave Smith, spent several months on silent retreat, and in 2017 completed the Community Dharma Leadership programme at Spirit Rock Meditation Center, which authorised him to teach. When Smith moved to Los Angeles in 2014, Andrew took over the day-to-day running of what was then Against the Stream Nashville, and he went on to lead and co-direct Wild Heart after it opened in East Nashville in 2017; he now sits on its teachers' council.

His talks treat the Buddha's teaching as practical wisdom for ordinary choices: the paramis or perfections such as truthfulness and equanimity, how thinking shapes experience, and setting intentions without demanding perfection. He leads Sunday morning meditation and discussion in rotation with another teacher, runs workshops and longer study courses, and co-leads silent residential retreats with Mikey Noechel. A licensed social worker, he has also built trainings that bring Buddhist and Western psychology into conversation for dedicated practitioners and for people working in education, and he has given guest lectures at universities around Nashville.

courses.title: The Unification of Mind: Cultivation of Samadhi Silent Meditation Retreat
courses.description: A five-day silent retreat in late January at St. Mary's Sewanee on the Cumberland Plateau, co-led with Mikey Noechel. The days are given to calming and collecting the attention so that clear seeing can arise from a settled mind.

courses.title: Sunday Morning Dharma & Discussion
courses.description: Wild Heart's early Sunday gathering in East Nashville, led by Andrew or Rachael Tanner-Smith: a guided sitting, a dharma talk and time for conversation. Anyone can drop in without registering.
